ours.name: Cathedral Traverse
ours.descent: Descend the Grand Teton by the Owen-Spalding route, with a rappel to the Upper Saddle, then down to the Lower Saddle. From there follow the climbers' path and then the trail down Garnet Canyon and back to the Lupine Meadows Trailhead.

fktText: Description Grand = Middle = South; Teton Trifecta (Summer version) Ascend the Grand Teton via the Owen Spalding Route, starting from the Lupine Meadows trailhead. From the summit of the Grand Teton make your way down to the lower saddle the same way you came up (the standard Owen Spalding Route). From the lower saddle follow the climbers trail south to the north side of the Middle Teton. Ascend the Middle Teton. We followed the climbers trail around a large horn to a prominent notch, downclimbed the notch and began climbing to our right (west) until we met the north facing couloir. We ascended the couloir roughly 100 vertical feet and then exited to the west on a ledge. We followed the ledge system to a low 5th class scramble and made our way to the top of the Middle Teton. From the summit of Middle Teton follow the standard trail down the southwest couloir to the saddle between Middle and South Teton. Proceed up South Teton via the standard route. Descend from the South Teton via the standard route (South-Middle Saddle Trail) until you reach Garnet Meadows. From Garnet Meadows follow the Garnet Canyon Trail back to trailhead where you originally came from. fktText: Description The Grand Teton – Modern Route Starting from Lupine Meadows Trailhead (6,732 ft), follow the Valley Trail toward the Amphitheater Lake Trail . At the 1.7-mile Junction , continue straight toward Amphitheater, Surprise, and Delta Lakes, up a series of well-built switchbacks. At the 3-mile Junction , take a sharp left onto the Garnet Canyon Trail , leading to Garnet Canyon and the high peaks. The trail climbs to the Boulder Field (4.0 mi / ~2,200 ft gain), a rugged section with great views of Garnet Canyon and the surrounding peaks. Then, navigate house-sized boulders to The Meadows (4.8 mi), where the designated trail ends. From here, ascend Northwest toward the Petzoldt Caves (5.1 mi / ~3,200 ft gain), following a maintained (but undesignated) trail. Past the caves, the trail reaches The Moraines and disappears into a maze of braided climber trails and moraine ridges, requiring careful route selection amid endless options. Climb steeply and carefully through The Moraines toward the Lower Saddle (6.4 mi / ~5,000 ft gain), guarded by Fixed Lines , a short climbing section, and more braided climber trails. (Note: Please be careful of rockfall here, and be conscientious of guided groups and other users.) From the Lower Saddle, the route becomes briefly "runnable" before the steep push to the Upper Saddle (7.2 mi / ~6,500 ft gain). fktText: Description This route is out of commission due to closed trails, refer to the new route - Grand Teton (Modern) The Grand Teton (13,770') is the second highest peak in Wyoming and one of the most iconic summits in the United States. It is a technical climb by any route. FKT attempts are usually by the Owen Spalding route (YDS 5.4), which also serves as the standard descent route. Bryce Thatcher, who held the FKT for the Grand for 29 years from 1983 until 2012, recounts some history of speed records on the Grand Teton here . Amazingly, just 10 days after Kilian Jornet finally bested Thatcher's record, Rocky Mountain National Park ranger Andy Anderson beat Jornet's time by just 59 seconds. An interview with Anderson on his Grand and Longs Peak (CO) records is on irunfar.com , and an outstanding podcast Episode with Andy is here on this website . The National Park Service has emphasized that cutting switchbacks on this route is a violation of the park service regulation 36 CFR 2.1(b), "Shortcutting a switchback along a trail is prohibited,". Any future attempts to cut switchbacks will result in complete rejection, and the NPS intends to pursue criminal charges against athletes who engage in this behavior. ours.name: Cirque of the Towers Traverse
ours.approach: From the Big Sandy trailhead, near 9,000 ft, take the Big Sandy trail (trail 99) past Big Sandy Lake and North Lake toward Jackass Pass; it is roughly 9 miles to Lonesome Lake. Above North Lake the trail steepens, and a cairned spur to the left leads toward Arrowhead Lake and the cirque, while the main trail crosses Jackass Pass (about 10,800 ft) and drops steeply to Lonesome Lake. Cross the cirque to Pingora's south shoulder, reached by a well-worn trail on the shoulder's west side; two short branches cut right onto the shoulder, class 3 at most. The traverse is usually begun on South Buttress: aim for the left side of the shoulder via third-class ramps, and the climbing begins at the crest
ours.descent: From the summit of Warbonnet, the last of the eleven peaks, continue south down a steep, loose ridge, then drop east into the scree basin between Arrowhead Lake and North Lake and pick up the Big Sandy Trail back toward camp and the trailhead.

fktText: Description A well established mountain adventure involving running for about 18 miles and climbing 3 miles along a world-class ridgeline. This one has been written up in the American Alpine Journal, Climbing Magazine, Cirque of the Towers Deep Lake rock climbing guide by Steve Bechtel and across the internet. It is undeniably classic for it's length, quality, and superb position on the Continental Divide at alpine elevations. This is not the usual fastestknowntime.com outing however, it involves rock climbing at 5.8 difficulty, objective hazards, extreme exposure, complex route finding, loose rock, and other hazards - rappelling is mandatory. The Cirque Traverse as it stands now, does meet all the parameters for inclusion in the annals of FKT.com. NOTE: As the FKT decreases where moving time is reduced but rappelling time largely stays the same, it may move outside the parameters of FKT.com route guidelines. The 2013 FKT logged about 50 minutes of rappelling - less than 10% of the total moving time. Access is via gravel and dirt roads (passenger cars okay) to the Big Sandy Trailhead on the Bridger-Teton National Forest in the southern Wind River Mountains. Imagine a diminutive Sierra Nevada mountain range with more mosquitos but fewer people...unless you head into the Cirque in peak summer. You are sure to make many new friends if you decide to go during peak season of July and August. Indeed, the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 broke mid-summer car parking records at the Big Sand

ours.name: Owen Spalding
ours.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle, pass left of the smooth pinnacle called the Needle and climb the gully close beside it (the tunnel known as the Eye of the Needle is optional); the scramble of roughly 1,400 ft to the Upper Saddle at about 13,160 ft is a serious undertaking in its own right. ours.name: Southwest Couloir
ours.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Climb the south fork all the way to the saddle between Middle and South Teton; do not branch off to the right early. From there the couloir is plainly visible to the west of the summit ridge. ours.descent: This couloir is the usual way down for the whole peak, so a party simply retraces the ascent to the saddle between Middle and South Teton. Go all the way past the saddle before turning east, because the snowfield northeast of it is steep early in the season.
